name: Jozabad
overview: Jozabad was a male warrior from the tribe of Manasseh who played a significant role during the time of King David. He is identified as a captain of thousands who defected to David, demonstrating his leadership and military influence. His arrival to David took place at Ziklag, marking a pivotal moment in David's consolidation of power.
namesAndTitles: The name Jozabad means 'YHWH bestowed,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's provision. This proper name, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 12:20, does not indicate it was given directly by God but carries a meaningful connection to divine blessing.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jozabad as a descendant of the tribe of Manasseh, situating him within this Israelite lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jozabad's significance lies in his leadership as a captain who chose to join David at Ziklag, signaling a critical shift of support toward David's kingship. His defection with his troops contributed to the strengthening of David's forces and the eventual establishment of his reign over Israel. This act of loyalty underscores the broader theme of God's providential guidance in David's rise.
